cards.title: What is a Design System?
cards.content:
A Design System is a complete set of standards, documentation, and reusable code components that guide design and development teams to build consistent digital products.

For React developers, a design system manifests as a package of reusable, accessible components (like Buttons, Inputs, and Modals) governed by global design rules.

cards.title: Design Tokens
cards.content:
Design Tokens are the visual atoms of a design system. They store raw values like colors, spacing, typography, and animation timing in a platform-agnostic format (usually JSON).

// tokens.json
{
  "color": {
    "brand-primary": "#0070f3",
    "gray-100": "#f4f4f4"
  },
  "spacing": {
    "small": "8px",
    "medium": "16px"
  }
}

In React, these tokens are consumed via CSS Variables, ThemeProviders, or CSS-in-JS configurations.

content.question: Which of the following is the primary purpose of Design Tokens?

options.text: To write performance testing scripts for production builds.
To maintain platform-agnostic visual values like colors, typography, and spacing for visual consistency.
To serve as automated databases for hosting user profile information.

cards.title: Implementing ThemeProvider
Component Isolation with Storybook
cards.content:
Storybook is a development environment and playground for UI components. It allows React developers to render components in total isolation from the main application, mocking props, context, and state variants.

This isolation ensures your design system components remain pure, reusable, and free of side-effects tied to global application state.

content.instruction: Put the steps for creating and documenting a React component in Storybook in the correct chronological order:

items.text: Create the presentation-only React component (e.g., Tag.tsx).
Write a Storybook file (Tag.stories.tsx) to define default metadata and template shapes.
Declare different story variations (e.g., Default, Large, Success) by passing different prop configurations.
Launch the local Storybook dashboard to interactively test states and edge cases.

content.instruction: Match each React and Design System concept to its correct architectural role:

pairs.right: A modular methodology breaking UI down into Atoms, Molecules, and Organisms.
Unstyled component primitives managing only state, interactions, and accessibility (e.g., Radix UI).
Passing utility tokens directly to components via style utilities (e.g., padding={4}).
Interactive UI panels allowing users to dynamically modify component props on the fly.

cards.title: Accessibility (a11y) in React
cards.content:
A design system's greatest advantage is bake-in accessibility (a11y). If the design system elements (e.g., modals, dropdowns) are compliant, all apps consuming them inherit compliance.

  • Use semantic HTML tags (<button> instead of <div onClick>).
  • Manage keyboard focus with tools like React Aria or Headless UI.
  • Add appropriate aria-* attributes to custom visual markup.

content.question: What is the primary benefit of utilizing 'headless' React utility libraries like Radix UI or Reach UI when coding a design system?

options.text: They automatically inject pre-written CSS styles matching your brand guidelines.
They provide highly optimized keyboard navigation, screen reader configurations, and DOM structure logic while leaving the styling completely to you.
They eliminate the need to write standard JavaScript code inside components.
